notes: The section a diff cannot produce at all, so the eval is mostly about the searching — and, since the reorder, about ROUTING. Section 4 now runs after the behaviour flows, so an affected entry a flow already explained belongs here as a named pointer and nothing more; only code no single flow owns is explained here. That is why whether an entry is RIGHT is graded in cases/behaviour-flows.json, where the explanation lives, and what is graded here is whether the pairing is complete, correctly routed and honestly searched. Presence of the lists is mechanical and lives in checks/blast-radius.sh, which also fails a reading order left in this section: that moved to section 3.

cases.expected_output: A blast-radius panel reaching from the new column to the unchanged query that scopes the selectable list, and two lists stacked one after the other, each the full measure. app/queries/active_projects.rb belongs to Flow B, so it appears as a named pointer to that flow rather than as an explanation. No reading order and no ranking of files: those live in section 3 now.
expectations: app/queries/active_projects.rb is in the affected list, and the search that found it is written down

At least one empty search is recorded as a search — an unrecorded absence cannot be told from an omission, and this diff has real ones (no other caller of archive!, no other reader of the archived scope)
The dashed nodes in the diagram are exactly the unchanged-and-affected ones, and the solid ones exactly the changed ones

Routing is right: an entry a flow already explains is a named pointer to that flow — a clause and a link, not the finding again with its citation and tier repeated. Anything explained in full here is genuinely owned by no single flow
It reads as a second pass rather than a first screen: it assumes the flows have been read, and does not re-teach the archival mechanism in order to make its own entries intelligible
The slug uniqueness validation appears as secondary work in a neutral register: independently reviewable, no criticism of the author for bundling it

expectations: web/src/queries/selectableProjects.ts is in the affected list and the search that found it is recorded
Affected code is found on both sides of the boundary, not only in api/ — a section that searched one side and stopped is the failure this fixture is built to catch
The diagram crosses the boundary rather than stopping at the serializer, and marks the unchanged client consumers as unchanged

Routing is right: the contract findings the flows own — the archivedAt key mismatch, the unhandled 422 — appear here as pointers into their flow, not as second explanations carrying the citation and tier again

Nothing in the section grades the change, scores it, or recommends a decision
